I’m still planting cotton on all 13.1 mu this year. I’ve grown it many years, and at my age I don’t want to change crops lightly when I know this land and this crop already. Cotton takes more watching and more hand labor at picking, but if I manage water and fertilizer in time, it still gives me steadier cash income than trying something unfamiliar. Some people in the family work off-farm, so I can’t count on everyone being home all the time. Because of that, I’ll keep the plan practical: plant in the usual window, use the seed type I know, put enough fertilizer so the crop does not look weak, and use the well for a few irrigations if the rain is not enough. I won’t push inputs too hard because pumping water and buying extra fertilizer both cost money, but I also don’t want to save too much and lose yield.

Before planting, I’ll have the field tilled and leveled like usual, then sow in mid to late April. I’ll use improved cotton seed from the local dealer, not the cheapest one, because with cotton if emergence is poor it is troublesome to fix later. For fertilizer, I’ll put most of it as base fertilizer, then add some topdressing later when the plants are growing strong. I usually listen to what experienced neighbors are doing, but I also look at my own field. If the plants stay pale, I’ll add a bit more nitrogen; if growth is already too lush, I’ll hold back so it doesn’t run to stalk. Water from the well is available, so I’ll irrigate a couple of times around key stages, but not too often because pumping costs money. Pesticide I will use only as needed, especially for insects and weeds, because cotton cannot be left unmanaged once pests come in.
